hypotheses.title: Named analog-field transfer (Dixie Valley, Brady, Desert Peak) on shared GeoDAWN + LiDAR layers
layers: INGENIOUS GDR 1391 well/spring unique cells whose names match Dixie / Brady / Desert Peak (owner-mirror CSV)
Published plant/area coordinates: OpenEI Dixie Valley, USGS MRDS Brady Hot Springs, OpenEI Desert Peak II
GeoDAWN bands: tmi_hg, tmi_vg, iso_grav_anom_hg, iso_grav_anom_slope, det_elev_slope, det_elev, depth_to_base_surf, geod_dilaterate, geod_shearrate, geod_2ndinv, cond_surf, mag_anom, rtp
LiDAR scarp channels: ex_max, step_max, lapneg_max, downface_max, upface_max, coh100
hypotheses.physical_signature: A classifier trained only on public-catalogue fault pixels inside named, densely explored geothermal fields, applied to the rest of the footprint; emission is off-catalogue analog-score ridges Poisson-thinned at d=2.8.
hypotheses.why_it_targets_faults_absent_from_USGS_I: Those fields have decades of industry drilling and denser mapping. A signature learned there might flag structurally similar, under-mapped traces elsewhere. It does not add independent extra-catalogue labels: source labels are still USGS/INGENIOUS inside the fields.
hypotheses.difference_from_prior_art: Prior work used the full regional catalogue or LiDAR globally. No reviewed artifact defined named Dixie/Brady/Desert Peak domains from GDR 1391 wells plus official centroids, measured a spatial-block domain discriminator, and emitted a unique off-catalogue analog-score field. GDR 1682/207 GIS payloads were not used (TLS blocked).
hypotheses.expected_DTI_improvement_rank: highest qualitative upside if domain shift were small; magnitude unknown a priori
hypotheses.implementation_cost: medium (implemented this session from already-restored rasters; no new external GIS)
hypotheses.specific_free_official_source: GDR 1391 https://gdr.openei.org/submissions/1391 ; OpenEI Dixie https://openei.org/wiki/Dixie_Valley_Geothermal_Area ; USGS MRDS Brady https://mrdata.usgs.gov/mrds/show-mrds.php?dep_id=10221999 ; OpenEI Desert Peak II https://openei.org/wiki/Desert_Peak_II_Geothermal_Facility ; Ben-David et al. 2010 https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10994-009-5152-4
hypotheses.obtainability_check: Official pages fetched 2026-10-04. Well/spring CSV is an owner-mirror of GDR 1391 (hash-pinned). GDR 1682 GIS and GDR 207 GIS_Faults.zip failed TLS (curl 35) and were not used. Named-field cells measured: Dixie 355,714 / Brady 172,283 / Desert Peak 100,324; union 527,997 with 7,848 catalogue pixels.
hypotheses.status: IMPLEMENTED; unique TIFF packaged; exploratory 20 km-block domain AUC 0.917; Ben-David bound NOT licensed (lambda unknown); P1 mean ΔDTI −0.093072 (0/4); P2 vs rebuilt C0 −0.016163; P2 vs matched-N random +0.001234; NOT_SLOT_CLEARED.

hypotheses.title: Conductive-surface linear edges coinciding with isostatic-gravity horizontal gradient, off-catalogue
layers: GeoDAWN cond_surf (band 17) and a Gaussian horizontal gradient of cond_surf
public catalogue used only as a 1-px exclusion mask, not as a training label
hypotheses.physical_signature: Ridge/NMS of electrical-conductivity surface gradient where gravity HG is also high. Geothermal fluids along faults create elongated conductors; gravity HG marks density contacts at range fronts and buried steps.
hypotheses.why_it_targets_faults_absent_from_USGS_I: USGS/INGENIOUS traces are surface ruptures. A conductivity lineament can mark a blind or fluid-filled structure that never produced a Quaternary scarp.
hypotheses.difference_from_prior_art: cond_surf is in the 19-band stack but was not used as a standalone linear-edge × gravity-HG conjunction in H19-5 packing, H27-4 pruning, C2 relays, or H33-F. H38-1 used heat-flow residual × Euler, not conductivity.
hypotheses.expected_DTI_improvement_rank: moderate if conductors are sparse and specific; otherwise low
hypotheses.specific_free_official_source: Competition training_features.tif band descriptions on https://www.drivendata.org/competitions/306/competition-doe-gems/page/967/ ; GeoDAWN https://www.usgs.gov/data/geodawn-airborne-magnetic-and-radiometric-surveys-northwestern-great-basin-nevada-and
hypotheses.obtainability_check: Band 17 is present in the owner-mirror training raster restored 2026-10-04. No new external download required.
hypotheses.status: NOT RUN. Do not implement as a slot candidate until a fold-safe P1/P2 proxy beats rebuilt C0.

hypotheses.title: Geodetic dilatation-rate edges × magnetic horizontal-gradient ridges, strike-discordant from the catalogue
layers: catalogue strike (local structure-tensor or nearest-trace azimuth) as a discordance gate
hypotheses.physical_signature: Active Basin-and-Range strain localizes on normal faults. Dilatation-rate edges mark hanging-wall/footwall transitions. Magnetic HG ridges whose azimuth differs from nearby mapped traces may be unmapped or newly activated structures.
hypotheses.why_it_targets_faults_absent_from_USGS_I: The public catalogue is a geologic surface-trace inventory, not a geodetic strain map. Discordant active-strain magnetic edges can exist without a compiled Quaternary trace.
hypotheses.difference_from_prior_art: H19-5 used geodetic bands as generic ensemble features. This hypothesis is a dilatation-edge × mag-HG conjunction with an explicit strike-discordance gate against the catalogue, which was not C2 (tip-to-tip relays) and not H33-F.
hypotheses.specific_free_official_source: GeoDAWN / INGENIOUS geodetic layers in training_features.tif; problem page https://www.drivendata.org/competitions/306/competition-doe-gems/page/967/
hypotheses.obtainability_check: Bands 3 and 8 restored 2026-10-04 in the owner-mirror stack. No new external data required.

hypotheses.title: LiDAR uphill-facing (antislope) scarp residual after removing catalogue-parallel steps
layers: lidar_scarp_features_u8.tif bands upface_max, strike, valid (USGS 3DEP 1 m aggregated)
public catalogue strike/distance as a suppression mask
hypotheses.physical_signature: Uphill-facing scarps can mark unrecognized faults, landslide headscarps, or lake shorelines. After suppressing steps whose strike is parallel to a nearby catalogue trace, residual upface ridges are candidate omitted faults.
hypotheses.why_it_targets_faults_absent_from_USGS_I: H19-5 already used LiDAR scarps supervised/packed toward the visible catalogue. Residuals that are antislope and strike-discordant are the part of the LiDAR field the catalogue-shaped emission is least likely to have spent.
hypotheses.difference_from_prior_art: H19-5 used LiDAR globally. This uses only the uphill-facing channel after catalogue-parallel suppression. Not the same as H27-4's 1-px flank prune.
hypotheses.expected_DTI_improvement_rank: low-to-moderate; confounded by landslides and shorelines
hypotheses.implementation_cost: medium (strike residual design + matched-random control required)
hypotheses.specific_free_official_source: USGS 3DEP 1 m DEM; lidar_scarp_features.json records USGS National Geospatial Program acknowledgement. Competition 1 m DEM links: https://www.drivendata.org/competitions/306/competition-doe-gems/data/
hypotheses.obtainability_check: Owner-mirror lidar_scarp_features_u8.tif restored 2026-10-04 (12 bands including upface_max). Official 3DEP tiles were not re-downloaded.

hypotheses.title: Volcanic-vent alignment corridors as hidden-fault priors
layers: gdr_volcanic_vents_in_footprint.csv (21 vents; owner-mirror of GDR 1391 volcanic features)
hypotheses.physical_signature: Basaltic vents in the Basin and Range often exploit hidden faults. Alignments of ≥3 vents define a corridor; magnetic/gravity ridges inside a narrow buffer and off-catalogue are the candidate traces.
hypotheses.why_it_targets_faults_absent_from_USGS_I: Vent locations are magmatic, not a Quaternary fault compilation. A vent-aligned magnetic ridge can mark a structure that never ruptured the surface in the mapped interval.
hypotheses.difference_from_prior_art: No reviewed GEMSDOE emission used the 21-vent CSV as an alignment prior. Distinct from hot-spring conjunctions (H35) and analog-field well polygons (H33-F).
hypotheses.expected_DTI_improvement_rank: low; n=21 vents, few alignments, easy to overfit
hypotheses.obtainability_check: CSV restored 2026-10-04, 21 rows, names null, rock types Basalt/Rhyolite. Official GDR payload not re-downloaded (TLS fail).
hypotheses.status: NOT RUN. Small-n; matched-random corridor control would be mandatory.

promotion_policy: A unique GeoTIFF may be packaged for format audit without being slot-approved. Slot approval still requires fold-safe candidate construction, P1 majority-fold gain vs the current-best comparable emission, non-loss on P2, and matched-random control when the operator changes count or placement. H33-F does not meet that gate.
